# Runtime Features — Epic Intake Brief

## Headline

Group the outstanding ToneForge demo milestones (Demo 10–16) and the remaining
runtime-related work items into a single tracking epic, so the runtime roadmap can
be prioritised, sequenced by dependency, and driven to completion.

## Problem statement

The remaining runtime and roadmap work is currently spread across many standalone
items plus a partially-populated epic. The epic description is a single paragraph
with no success criteria, and its stated contents do not match its actual children
(the "machine-use demo" is referenced but is not a child). Without a well-defined
grouping epic it is hard to see what remains, what is blocked, and in what order the
work must land.

## Users

- **ToneForge producers/maintainers** who need one place to track and prioritise the
  outstanding demo milestones and runtime enhancements.
- **Implementing engineers/agents** who need the group's boundary, dependency order,
  and definition of done.

Example user stories:

- As a producer, I want the remaining runtime/roadmap features grouped under one epic
  with explicit dependencies, so that I can see what is blocked and sequence work.
- As an engineer, I want each child of the epic to carry a clear goal and measurable
  acceptance criteria, so that I can pick up a child and know when it is done.
- As a maintainer, I want the runtime module to eventually produce audible output in
  a meaningful demo, so that the runtime's value is demonstrable end-to-end.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every direct child of this epic reaches a terminal stage (`in_review` or
   `completed`); the epic itself is advanced to `in_review` only once all children
   are terminal and blockers are resolved.
2. Each direct child has a clear goal and measurable acceptance criteria, verified by
   the shared tree-coverage review (`run_coverage_review`) returning `proceed` for the
   epic.
3. Inter-child dependency edges are recorded via `wl dep` and honoured in execution
   order (prerequisites first, per `docs/prd/DEMO_ROADMAP.md`).
4. The runtime PRD revisit (TF-0MM4M1NXU0WHH6AJ) is resolved: `docs/prd/RUNTIME_PRD.md`
   defines how the runtime wires into the render/playback pipeline, and the resulting
   audio-producing runtime demo has a clear, verifiable audible-output user story.
5. The epic's child inventory accurately reflects its actual children (no phantom
   entries; any item referenced as a child must genuinely be parented to this epic).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Scope

**In scope**

- Grouping and dependency maintenance for Demo 10–16 and the runtime enhancements
  listed as children.
- Resolving the runtime PRD revisit and defining the audio-producing runtime demo.
- Reconciling the epic's stated contents with its actual children.

**Out of scope**

- Implementing any child feature (each child owns its own implementation).
- New runtime/roadmap features not already represented by a child.
- Promotion to `main`/release (owned by the `ship` skill).

## Constraints

- Demo sequencing follows `docs/prd/DEMO_ROADMAP.md`; blocked children stay blocked
  until their prerequisites complete.
- The runtime PRD (`docs/prd/RUNTIME_PRD.md`) is authoritative for runtime behaviour;
  the epic must not invent behaviour that contradicts it.
- Manual/curated PRDs in `docs/prd/` are the source of product intent.

## Existing state

- Epic is `issueType: epic`, `priority: low`, `stage: idea`, `status: in-progress`
  (claimed for this intake), assignee `Map`.
- 14 direct children exist (see disposition table below); Demo 11–16 are `blocked` on
  prerequisites, the rest are `open`.
- `src/runtime/` orchestrates state/context/sequence presets but does not itself
  produce audio; the previous Demo 9 was removed for logging simulated transitions
  only.
- `README.md` and `docs/prd/DEMO_ROADMAP.md` describe the overall demo sequence.

### Child inventory & intake disposition

| Child | Title | Status | Stage | Intake disposition |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TF-0MLXF8ZW21HJLFOG | Demo 10: Mixer | open | plan_complete | Past intake; 3 clarifying questions still open (see Appendix Q2) |
| TF-0MMLC8B3T0Z1F7ZM | Mixer runtime foundation | open | idea | Needs brief; blocked on Appendix Q2 |
| TF-0MMLC8PXU0D3O594 | Mixer rule config loader | open | idea | Needs brief; blocked on Appendix Q2 |
| TF-0MMLC8SQ302DVYOZ | Mixer voice limiting tests | open | idea | Needs brief; blocked on Appendix Q2 |
| TF-0MLXF98WZ1LQGM5W | Demo 11: Intelligence | blocked | idea | Well-defined; cannot be intake'd while blocked on Demo 7 & 10 |
| TF-0MLXF9FWG18T2ZHD | Demo 12: Compiler & Validator | blocked | idea | Well-defined; blocked on Demo 7 & 11 |
| TF-0MLXF9O241QG5APK | Demo 13: Visualizer & Haptics | blocked | idea | Well-defined; blocked on Demo 9 & 10 |
| TF-0MMN7O97300JWHEW | Demo 13A: Visualizer | open | idea | Well-defined (has user story + ACs) |
| TF-0MMN7O9901NGG0NA | Demo 13B: Haptics | open | idea | Well-defined (has user story + ACs) |
| TF-0MLXFB8R61P63G4B | Demo 14: Intent & Memory | blocked | idea | Well-defined; blocked on Demo 11 |
| TF-0MLXFBHHW1BBO1ZJ | Demo 15: Network & Integrations | blocked | idea | Well-defined; blocked on Demo 9 & 12 |
| TF-0MLXFBLNF1MCYS6Y | Demo 16: Marketplace | blocked | idea | Well-defined; blocked on Demo 12 & 15 |
| TF-0MLYX9DP51U7AQDK | Realtime adjustment of parameters | open | idea | Needs product definition (see Appendix Q3) |
| TF-0MM4M1NXU0WHH6AJ | Revisit runtime PRD | open | idea | Well-defined (has user story + ACs) |

### Discrepancies found

- The epic description names **"the machine-use demo"** as a child, but
  TF-0MLYUG79Y1KMDPMI ("Machine use demo", `feature`, `intake_complete`,
  `needsProducerReview: true`) has **no parent** — it is not a child of this epic.
- Blocked children (Demo 11–16) cannot be claimed for intake without erasing their
  `blocked` status, so their per-child intake pass cannot run until prerequisites
  complete. Their descriptions are already detailed.

## Desired change

- Finalise this epic's goal, users, success criteria, scope, and constraints as above.
- Reconcile the child inventory (either re-parent the machine-use demo, or correct the
  description to remove the reference).
- Run the per-child intake pass for the four under-defined open children once the
  Appendix questions are answered, advancing them to `intake_complete`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/prd/DEMO_ROADMAP.md` — canonical demo sequence and dependencies.
- `docs/prd/RUNTIME_PRD.md` — runtime behaviour to be revisited by TF-0MM4M1NXU0WHH6AJ.
- `docs/prd/MIXER_PRD.md` — Mixer concepts underlying the Demo 10 children.
- `src/runtime/runtime.ts` — runtime module referenced by the PRD revisit.
- `config/mixer/*.json` — proposed declarative Mixer rules location (unconfirmed, see Appendix Q2).
- `README.md` — roadmap/feature overview to keep in sync.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: scope creep.** Adding new runtime/roadmap features to this grouping epic
  expands it indefinitely. *Mitigation:* record any new opportunity as a separate work
  item (child if it blocks, otherwise `discovered-from`) rather than widening this epic.
- **Risk: phantom children / stale description** misleads prioritisation.
  *Mitigation:* reconcile the child inventory (AC 5).
- **Risk: blocked children are intake'd prematurely**, erasing `blocked` status.
  *Mitigation:* only intake blocked children after prerequisites complete.
- **Assumption:** the epic's purpose is tracking/grouping, not delivering a single
  new capability; completion is defined by its children reaching terminal stage.
- **Assumption:** the rules file path and mix-group list proposed by the prior Demo 10
  intake remain unconfirmed (Appendix Q2).

## Related work (manual)

- `docs/prd/DEMO_ROADMAP.md` — the demo sequence this epic tracks.
- TF-0MUUB39EL000YCT0 "Make ToneForge Runtime-aware (browser-compatible playback)"
  (`in-progress`, `in_review`) — directly advances runtime playback; not currently a
  child of this epic.
- TF-0MUV748IA0028PVO "Browser e2e: pre-existing terminal/wizard failures"
  (`in-progress`) — related browser demo/reliability work.
- TF-0MLYUG79Y1KMDPMI "Machine use demo" — referenced as a child but unparented.
- TF-0MLXF8TBT0DJDCO1 "Demo 9: Runtime & State" (`completed`) — prerequisite of
  Demo 10/13/15, and the source of the runtime PRD revisit item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

> All questions below are **OPEN QUESTION** — awaiting producer input. Intake cannot be
> finalised until they are answered.

- **Q1 (epic definition).** How should this grouping epic measure success?
  - (A) Meta-epic: success = every child reaches a terminal stage (recommended, matches
    the description's grouping intent).
  - (B) Deliverable epic: it must itself own a concrete runtime deliverable beyond its
    children.
  - **Recommended:** A — the description clearly frames this as a grouping/tracking epic.
  - **OPEN QUESTION** — no answer yet.

- **Q2 (Demo 10 / Mixer children).** The prior Demo 10 intake left three questions
  unanswered that also block the three Mixer children:
  1. Confirm the rules file path: `config/mixer/*.json`? (Yes / Different path)
  2. Confirm the mix group list: footsteps, UI, combat, ambience, dialogue, alerts?
     (Yes / Add/Remove)
  3. Add Demo 9 (Runtime & State) as a blocking dependency now, or leave to a Producer?
  - **OPEN QUESTION** — no answer yet. Blocks TF-0MMLC8B3T0Z1F7ZM,
    TF-0MMLC8PXU0D3O594, TF-0MMLC8SQ302DVYOZ.

- **Q3 ("Realtime adjustment of parameters", TF-0MLYX9DP51U7AQDK).** What is the
  intended scope?
  - (A) Real-time modulation of a *specific* parameter set (e.g. engine RPM/pitch) for
    continuous sounds only.
  - (B) General real-time parameter automation for any playing sound.
  - (C) Out of scope for this epic; move to its own item.
  - **Recommended:** A — the description names engine noise as the motivating example,
    implying a focused continuous-sound use case.
  - **OPEN QUESTION** — no answer yet.

- **Q4 (child reconciliation).** The description lists "the machine-use demo" as a
  child, but TF-0MLYUG79Y1KMDPMI is unparented.
  - (A) Re-parent TF-0MLYUG79Y1KMDPMI under this epic.
  - (B) Correct the parent description to remove the reference (keep it standalone).
  - **Recommended:** B — the machine-use demo is a self-contained CLI reporting demo
    (`intake_complete`) and is not runtime/demo-roadmap work in the same sense.
  - **OPEN QUESTION** — no answer yet.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **TF-0MLXF8TBT0DJDCO1** – Demo 9: Runtime & State -- Real-Time Behavioral Sound (completed)
- **TF-0MMN7O97300JWHEW** – Demo 13A: Visualizer -- Cross-Modal Output (open)
- **TF-0MM17DY5N1R83EOF** – Add global run guard to prevent concurrent step execution (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `standups/2026_10_05.md` — matched: children, demo, demos, feature, features (+8 more)
- `README.md` — matched: blocked, demo, demos, feature, features (+5 more)
- `docs/prd/DEMO_ROADMAP.md` — matched: demo, demos, machine, open, prd (+5 more)

## Summary

The completed work item TF-0MN06817414DW638 (Remove Tone.js dependency and unify on buildOfflineGraph) removed Tone.js from the codebase, but package.json still lists tone as a dependency. This item covers verifying and removing that leftover entry.

## Problem

package.json (root) still contains:
  tone: ^15.1.22
in the dependencies section. The web package previously also depended on tone.

If Tone.js is genuinely unused, this is dead weight that increases install size and may confuse contributors about the rendering architecture.

## Implementation

1. Verify no source file imports tone (grep for tone imports).
2. Verify the web package no longer imports tone.
3. Remove tone from package.json dependencies (root and web, if present).
4. Run npm install to update the lockfile.
5. Confirm the full test suite and web build still pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. No file in the project imports tone
2. tone does not appear in any package.json dependency list
3. npm install completes cleanly and the lockfile is updated
4. Full test suite passes
5. Web build succeeds

## Key Files

- package.json (root)
- web/package.json
- package-lock.json
